cohort: The study included 69 women who underwent cesarean delivery at a hospital in Moradabad, India.
finding: The prevalence of isthmocele was 13% at 6 weeks post-cesarean, decreasing to 7.7% at 6 months, with trends suggesting higher incidence in women with retroverted uterus and single-layer uterine closure.
mod_finding: The study specifically investigates risk factors for isthmocele *after* cesarean section, finding that surgical technique (single-layer uterine closure) and uterine orientation may influence its development.
